title: Student Mental Health & Wellness Tasks
description: These tasks address academic stress, exam anxiety, social pressures, financial worries, imposter syndrome, and future uncertainty while building resilience, confidence, and healthy study habits.

tasks.task: Practice the '5-minute brain dump' before studying to clear mental clutter and anxiety.
Use positive self-talk before exams: 'I am prepared and capable of handling this challenge.'
Take a 10-minute walk between study sessions to reset your focus and reduce mental fatigue.
Practice the 'academic anxiety reset' - deep breathing when overwhelmed by coursework.
Keep a 'wins journal' of academic achievements, no matter how small, to combat imposter syndrome.
Use the 'pomodoro with intention' - set a positive intention before each 25-minute study block.
Practice gratitude for your opportunity to learn when feeling overwhelmed by coursework.
Create a 'calm corner' in your dorm/room with comfort items for stress relief.
Use the 'test anxiety toolkit' - breathing exercises, positive affirmations, and grounding techniques.
Practice the 'comparison detox' - limit social media when feeling inadequate about others' success.
Keep a 'growth mindset journal' - write about challenges as opportunities to improve.
Use the 'perfectionism pause' - ask 'Is this good enough?' to prevent endless revisions.
Practice 'study session meditation' - 2 minutes of breathing before opening textbooks.
Create a 'future self visualization' to stay motivated during difficult academic periods.
Use the 'academic overwhelm SOS' - break large tasks into tiny, manageable steps.
Practice loving-kindness meditation for classmates you feel competitive with.
Keep a 'learning joy list' of subjects or topics that genuinely excite you.
Use the 'grade grief process' - allow yourself to feel disappointed, then move forward.
Practice the 'imposter syndrome antidote' - list three things you've genuinely learned this week.
Create a 'stress release playlist' for post-exam emotional decompression.
